The draft asked about MAY 2026 expecting a real zero; May holds ZERO of 31 days — a ~26-day capture HOLE (April stops at the 5th, rows resume in June) — so the original question would have graded a hole refusal as a false-zero failure. assert.rubric: CERTIFIED FROM THE WAREHOUSE 2026-08-15: Foam OH google account grain, 2026-07-01..2026-07-31 = 31 of 31 days present, spend $0.00 · 0 impressions · 0 clicks · 0 conversions. Coverage is COMPLETE and the zero is REAL — every day of the window was captured and every one of them says zero. A passing answer states the zero plainly (the account did not run Google ads in July 2026) WITHOUT hedging it into 'we may not have the data'. ⛔ THIS QUESTION IS THE DELIBERATE PAIR TO H1-3, AND THE PAIRING IS THE POINT: same shape of question, opposite correct answer — H1-3's window is a capture hole where a zero would be a lie, this one is complete coverage where refusing to state the zero is over-refusal. A model that gets both right has the distinction; one that gets both 'safe' has only learned to refuse. ⚠ PRECISION FOR THE JUDGE: this is a DENSITY-complete zero, not a VENDOR-ATTESTED one — walk attestation (outcome='zero') covers only 2026-08-09..12, so an answer claiming Google itself confirmed the zero is over-claiming; 'we captured every day and every day was zero' is the accurate ground.

assert.rubric: THE A6 CASE. Two halves, both required. The registry's own sentence is the model: 'we have not established a search-term-specific wall; the general 37-month granular window applies as far as we know.'
